title: Veterans Pension One-Time Payment Declaration — Amount Declared
content:
**Clause — amount of a Veterans Pension one-time payment declaration.** The declaration is the one-time amount counted, rounded to the cent. In the declaration:

- the period covered is the 12 whole months before the declaration;
- the releases are the retroactive Disability Compensation releases deposited to the veteran in that period, taken at their gross amount;
- the representative's fee is left in the releases;
- the part of a release withheld to repay a VA debt was paid on the veteran's behalf and stays in the declared amount;
- the releases are taken as paid only for months the pension was also paid, so they are settled against the pension and nothing is counted.

## Reading the clause

| Question | Answer under the clause |
|---|---|
| Which releases are looked at? | those deposited in the 12 whole months before the declaration |
| At what amount? | gross, with the representative's fee and any debt withholding left in |
| How much of them counts? | none — settled against the pension |
| Declared amount | 0.00 |

## Hypothetical illustration

Two retroactive releases deposited 4 and 7 whole months before the declaration, of 3000.00 and 5000.00 gross, with 600.00 withheld from the second to repay a VA debt: the releases in the period total 8000.00 gross, the withholding staying in. Settled against the pension, nothing counts, and the declaration is 0.00.
